title: Region loss and traffic shift
description: Walk a region outage. DNS/anycast shift is not a lossless cutover of a single-primary database. RPO is the replication you actually had.
assumptions: Active-passive SQL primary in region A with async replica in region B unless a step says sync majority.
DynamoDB global tables and Cosmos-style multi-master are a different conflict story — not silently mixed in.
TokenX single-writer ledger does not become multi-master because DNS flipped.

steps.title: Healthy dual region
steps.timeline: t0: writes in region A. Replica in B lagged (example: 0.5–5 s async). Reads may be local-with-lag.
steps.inFlight: Writes wait on A. Cross-region reads optional.
steps.consistency: B is not linearizable with A under async.
steps.durability: Acknowledged on A. On B only after apply.
steps.userVisible: Local read latency in B if you allowed stale.
steps.recovery: Measure lag continuously. Lag is the RPO.

steps.title: Detect region A loss
steps.timeline: t1: A is unreachable (AZ/region event). Health and DNS still advertise A until TTL/health.
steps.consistency: No writer if you do not promote. Stale B reads if you fail open reads.
steps.durability: Unreplicated tail on A is the RPO.
steps.userVisible: Errors for writes. Reads depend on policy.
steps.recovery: Human or automated fence of A before B writes.

steps.title: In-flight cross-region
steps.timeline: t1–t2: commits on A not on B.
steps.inFlight: UNKNOWN to clients. Those rows may be gone if A never returns and B is promoted.
steps.consistency: Do not read B as proof A failed the commit.
steps.durability: RPO > 0 for async. Sync majority across regions is a different latency tax you must have paid before.
steps.userVisible: Money APIs must say UNKNOWN, not declined.
steps.recovery: Idempotent retry after a new epoch only if the key store survived.

steps.title: Promote region B
steps.timeline: t2: fence A (disable routes, revoke lease). Promote B. DNS/anycast cutover.
steps.inFlight: DNS TTL still sends some traffic to A.
steps.consistency: New epoch. Old A must not accept writes if it returns.
steps.durability: Tail lost if async. That is not an instantaneous, lossless cutover.
steps.userVisible: Write errors until cutover; then possible missing last seconds of data.
steps.recovery: STONITH equivalent for the old region’s writer.

steps.title: Clients follow DNS
steps.timeline: t2–t3: retries hit B with same keys.
steps.inFlight: Keys applied on B if the original never committed on B — correct. If A had committed and later heals, conflict.
steps.userVisible: Success after retry or persistent UNKNOWN if key state lost.
steps.recovery: Sticky regional identity in the key.

steps.title: Conflict if A returns
steps.timeline: t3: A heals with unreplicated commits.
steps.inFlight: Must rewind A or reconcile row-by-row. Not automatic.
steps.durability: Backups of A may hold the only copy of the tail — restore vs discard is a business call.
steps.userVisible: Possible missing transfers vs duplicate — this is why TokenX is single-writer.
steps.recovery: Run reconciliation. Ads can drop a window; money cannot guess.

steps.title: Rebuild topology
steps.timeline: t4: new replica in healed A. Lag catch-up from B.
steps.consistency: A is derived replica until you fail back with another fence.
steps.durability: Failback is another promotion event with the same eight steps.
steps.recovery: Game-day this path. DNS TTL is part of RTO.

steps.title: User-visible outcome
steps.timeline: End: writes in B, RPO of async tail, RTO of detect+fence+DNS.
steps.userVisible: Outage minutes, possible lost un-replicated writes, successful keyed retries.
steps.recovery: If you needed RPO=0 you needed sync majority and its latency before the incident.
